Email Retention Policy

Retention

Mailboxes are retained for 2 years after an employee leaves, then permanently deleted.

Classification and filing

Email is a communication channel, not an indefinite records store. A message evidencing a care,
employment, contractual, complaint, safeguarding or governance decision is transferred promptly to the
approved record system and classified under the applicable retention schedule. Routine coordination,
duplicates, alerts and transient working messages are deleted when no longer needed.

Retention and disposal

Mailbox retention settings support, but do not replace, the duty to file a business record correctly.
Automatic deletion is suspended for a legal hold, investigation, subject-access search or other authorised
preservation requirement. When the hold ends, disposal resumes under the relevant schedule and is
recorded where the record class requires evidence of destruction.

Access and assurance

Managers arrange controlled mailbox access for absence, leavers or investigations through the
documented authorisation route; passwords are never shared. Information Governance reviews retention
configuration, preservation holds and exception reports at least annually. Staff report misdirected sensitive
email immediately under the Data Breach Procedure rather than attempting to resolve it silently.

Falls Prevention Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group assesses falls risk and responds when a resident falls. It applies to every resident, with particular attention to a resident identified as being at higher risk.

Policy statement

Falls prevention balances a resident's right to move around freely with a proportionate response to their individual risk, since an overly restrictive approach can itself cause harm by reducing a resident's mobility, confidence and independence.

Definitions

**Falls risk assessment** the structured assessment completed for every resident at admission and reviewed regularly thereafter. **Post-fall protocol** the immediate response steps followed after any fall, regardless of apparent severity. **On-call registered manager** the manager reachable out of hours, who is the escalation contact for a fall under this version.

Roles and responsibilities

**Care staff** follow the post-fall protocol immediately after any fall and contact the on-call registered manager. **The registered manager** reviews the falls risk assessment after any fall and updates the care plan accordingly. **The GP or emergency services** are contacted where the post-fall protocol indicates a possible injury requiring clinical assessment.

Complete a falls risk assessment at admission and review it at least every three months, or sooner following any fall.

Following any fall, do not move the resident until a basic check for obvious injury has been completed, unless leaving them in place presents its own risk.

Contact the on-call registered manager immediately after any fall, regardless of whether an injury is apparent.

Call emergency services immediately for a suspected serious injury, such as a suspected fracture or head injury with loss of consciousness.

Record every fall, including one without apparent injury, in the resident's care record and the site's falls log.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a resident falls in a public area of the site with other residents present, staff prioritise the fallen resident's safety and dignity first, managing the immediate area calmly rather than treating other residents' reactions as the first concern.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a resident falls in a public area of the site with other residents present, staff prioritise the fallen resident's safety and dignity first, managing the immediate area calmly rather than treating other residents' reactions as the first concern.

Local and regional variations

Harbour View's higher proportion of residents with complex mobility needs means it holds a dedicated falls prevention equipment store, including a range of mobility aids not routinely stocked at smaller sites.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This policy works alongside the Incident Reporting Policy (governing the wider incident record a fall also triggers) and the CQC Notification Procedure (governing when a fall meets the notifiable serious injury threshold).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the escalation standard. A resident is found on the floor of their room during a night shift, with no obvious injury visible. The care assistant completes the basic injury check, contacts the on-call registered manager as required, and together they decide the resident can be safely assisted back to bed, with the fall recorded in full and the risk assessment scheduled for review the next working day.

Frequently asked questions

**Does every fall need a GP review, even without apparent injury?** Not automatically, but the on-call registered manager considers this on a case-by-case basis, and a pattern of repeated falls prompts a GP review regardless of any single fall's apparent severity. **Can a family member be told about a fall immediately, even at night?** Yes, where the family has asked to be informed of any fall regardless of time, this preference is recorded and followed.

Training and competency

All care staff complete falls prevention and post-fall protocol training at induction, refreshed annually, including manual handling relevant to assisting a resident safely after a fall.

Monitoring and compliance

Falls data is reviewed monthly by the registered manager, looking for a pattern by resident, time of day, or location that might indicate an environmental or care plan factor worth addressing.

Record keeping and retention

Falls log entries and updated risk assessments are retained in the resident's care record per the Records Retention Schedule.

Approval and review history

This policy was originally approved by the Chief Executive on 1 March 2025 and was superseded by a later version, described in that version's own record, effective 1 April 2026.

Environmental factors in falls prevention

Beyond the individual risk assessment, the registered manager reviews environmental factors across the site — lighting, flooring, clutter and appropriate footwear availability — as part of a wider falls prevention approach, since a purely individual-level assessment can miss a hazard affecting several residents at once.

Debriefing after a fall with the resident

Where the resident is able to take part, staff gently discuss what happened after a fall once they are settled and comfortable, since the resident's own account can reveal a contributing factor, such as reaching for something out of easy reach, that would not otherwise be captured in the formal record.

Footwear and clothing considerations

Staff check that a resident's footwear is well-fitted and appropriate for their mobility level as part of routine care, since loose slippers or an unfamiliar new pair of shoes are a common, easily overlooked contributing factor in an otherwise unexplained fall.

Falls prevention equipment and its correct use

Equipment such as a sensor mat, a low bed, or a grab rail is provided based on the individual risk assessment, and staff are shown how to use each item correctly for the specific resident it is provided for, since incorrectly positioned or unused equipment provides no real protection despite appearing to address the identified risk.

Medication review as a falls prevention measure

The GP or pharmacist reviews a resident's medication periodically with falls risk specifically in mind, since certain medications, or a recent change in dose, can affect balance or alertness in a way that meaningfully raises falls risk independent of any physical or environmental factor already identified.

Supporting a resident's confidence after a fall

Beyond the physical response, staff pay attention to a resident's confidence following a fall, since a fear of falling again can itself lead a resident to reduce their own activity in a way that increases longer-term risk; gentle encouragement back toward their usual level of activity, rather than an assumption that reduced activity is automatically the safer choice, is part of a genuinely proportionate response.

Closing note

A proportionate, well-practised response to a fall protects a resident far more than an overly cautious restriction on their everyday movement, and this policy exists to keep that balance right in practice, not only in principle.

Falls Prevention Policy

Supersedes the version effective 1 March 2025. Adds the falls lead nurse or therapist as a mandatory escalation contact, alongside the on-call registered manager, for any fall with suspected injury.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group assesses falls risk and responds when a resident falls. It applies to every resident, with particular attention to a resident identified as being at higher risk.

Policy statement

Falls prevention balances a resident's right to move around freely with a proportionate response to their individual risk, since an overly restrictive approach can itself cause harm by reducing a resident's mobility, confidence and independence.

Definitions

**Falls risk assessment** the structured assessment completed for every resident at admission and reviewed regularly thereafter. **Post-fall protocol** the immediate response steps followed after any fall, regardless of apparent severity. **Falls lead** the nurse or therapist now designated at each site as a mandatory escalation contact, alongside the on-call registered manager, for any fall with suspected injury.

Roles and responsibilities

**Care staff** follow the post-fall protocol immediately after any fall and contact the on-call registered manager, and now also the falls lead where injury is suspected. **The registered manager** reviews the falls risk assessment after any fall and updates the care plan accordingly. **The falls lead** provides a clinical assessment for any suspected-injury fall, a new role introduced in this version, working alongside the GP or emergency services where further escalation is needed.

Complete a falls risk assessment at admission and review it at least every three months, or sooner following any fall.

Following any fall, do not move the resident until a basic check for obvious injury has been completed, unless leaving them in place presents its own risk.

Contact the on-call registered manager immediately after any fall, regardless of whether an injury is apparent.

Where injury is suspected, also contact the falls lead immediately, in addition to the on-call registered manager; this dual-contact requirement is new in this version and was not required previously.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where the falls lead is not immediately reachable following a suspected-injury fall, the on-call registered manager proceeds with emergency services contact where warranted without waiting, and the falls lead is updated as soon as they become available, since the new dual-contact step is additive and never delays an emergency response.

Local and regional variations

Harbour View's higher proportion of residents with complex mobility needs means it holds a dedicated falls prevention equipment store, including a range of mobility aids not routinely stocked at smaller sites, and its falls lead role is filled by a permanent on-site physiotherapist given the site's larger nursing capacity.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This policy works alongside the Incident Reporting Policy (governing the wider incident record a fall also triggers) and the CQC Notification Procedure (governing when a fall meets the notifiable serious injury threshold).

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the new dual-contact standard. A resident is found on the floor of their room during a night shift, with a suspected wrist injury visible on the basic check. The care assistant contacts both the on-call registered manager and the falls lead, as this version now requires for a suspected-injury fall, and the falls lead's clinical input helps determine that a GP review rather than an emergency department visit is the appropriate next step.

All care staff complete falls prevention and post-fall protocol training at induction, refreshed annually, updated to cover when falls lead contact is required, including manual handling relevant to assisting a resident safely after a fall.

Record keeping and retention

Missing Person Procedure

1. Immediate search

A 30-minute site and immediate-grounds search is conducted before escalating further.

2. Police contact

If not found after the immediate search, police are called on 101 (or 999 if there is immediate risk).

Immediate response

Staff confirm the person is not elsewhere on site, note the last verified sighting, clothing, mobility,
communication needs and likely destinations, and preserve relevant CCTV or access records. The
registered manager assesses immediate vulnerability and calls emergency services without delay where
risk is high; local searching never postpones a necessary police report.

Search and communication

The search is coordinated, logged and allocated so unsafe duplication and unsearched areas are visible.
Staff maintain safe staffing for residents who remain on site. Family, commissioners and safeguarding
contacts are informed according to the person's plan and the circumstances, while public communication
and photographs are released only through the police-led or otherwise authorised route.

Return and learning

On return, immediate welfare and medical needs are assessed before a calm account is sought. The care
plan, risk assessment and known triggers are reviewed with the person and relevant representatives. The
incident record includes timings, decisions, notifications and search activity, and repeated episodes or
control failures are escalated for safeguarding and service-level review.

Staff Benefits Guidance

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains the retail discount scheme available to Alderbridge staff. It applies to every member of staff across every site.

Policy statement

Staff can access a retail discount scheme offering typically 5-10% off at participating retailers, a straightforward benefit available to every staff member from their start date.

Definitions

**Participating retailer** a retailer that has agreed to offer the scheme's discount to an Alderbridge staff member. **Scheme provider** the third-party company that administers the discount scheme and its list of participating retailers.

1. Register for the discount scheme through the staff portal using a personal email address.
2. Browse the current list of participating retailers and their specific discount rate, typically 5-10%, through the scheme provider's own platform.
3. Present the scheme's digital or physical card, as the retailer requires, at the point of purchase to receive the discount.
4. Report any issue redeeming a discount to HR, who liaises with the scheme provider on the staff member's behalf.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Long Service Recognition Scheme and the pension scheme guidance as part of the wider set of staff benefits Alderbridge offers.

Worked example

A worked example illustrates typical use. A staff member registers for the scheme in their first week, browses the participating retailer list, and uses the discount card for a purchase at a participating supermarket, receiving the retailer's specific discount rate within the 5-10% range the scheme offers.

Frequently asked questions

**Does the discount scheme cost anything for a staff member to join?** No, it is a free benefit provided by Alderbridge. **Does an agency worker have access to the discount scheme?** No, it is available to a direct Alderbridge employee only.

Promoting the scheme

HR promotes the discount scheme periodically through the staff newsletter and at induction, since a genuinely useful benefit provides little value if staff are not aware it exists or have forgotten how to access it since their initial registration.

Feedback on the scheme

Staff feedback on the discount scheme, including a suggestion for a retailer not currently participating, is welcomed by HR and passed to the scheme provider to consider, since the scheme is more valuable to staff when it reflects the retailers they actually want to use.

Closing note

A simple, genuinely useful discount scheme is a small but real way Alderbridge supports staff day to day, and this guidance exists to make it easy to find and use.

Staff Benefits Guidance

*Supersedes the version effective 1 April 2025. New scheme provider, wider discount range.*

Purpose and scope

This guidance explains the retail discount scheme available to Alderbridge staff. It applies to every member of staff across every site.

Policy statement

Staff can access a retail discount scheme offering typically 5-15% off at a wider range of participating retailers, following a change of scheme provider, a straightforward benefit available to every staff member from their start date.

Definitions

**Participating retailer** a retailer that has agreed to offer the scheme's discount to an Alderbridge staff member, now a wider range following the provider change. **Scheme provider** the third-party company that administers the discount scheme and its list of participating retailers, changed in this version.

1. Register for the discount scheme through the staff portal using a personal email address; an existing registration under the previous provider is migrated automatically.
2. Browse the current, wider list of participating retailers and their specific discount rate, now typically 5-15%, through the new scheme provider's platform.
3. Present the scheme's digital or physical card, as the retailer requires, at the point of purchase to receive the discount.
4. Report any issue redeeming a discount to HR, who liaises with the new scheme provider on the staff member's behalf.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This guidance works alongside the Long Service Recognition Scheme and the pension scheme guidance as part of the wider set of staff benefits Alderbridge offers.

Worked example

A worked example illustrates the wider range now available. A staff member who previously found few participating retailers relevant to them checks the new, wider list following the provider change, and finds a retailer they regularly use now participates at a 12% discount, within the new 5-15% range this version introduces.

Frequently asked questions

worked example illustrates the wider range now available. A staff member who previously found few participating retailers relevant to them checks the new, wider list following the provider change, and finds a retailer they regularly use now participates at a 12% discount, within the new 5-15% range this version introduces.

Frequently asked questions

**Why did the scheme provider change?** A review found the new provider offers a meaningfully wider retailer range and higher typical discount; existing staff registrations were migrated automatically. **Does a staff member need to re-register after the provider change?** No, migration was automatic, though staff are encouraged to log in and confirm their details are current.

Promoting the scheme

HR promotes the discount scheme periodically through the staff newsletter and at induction, now highlighting the wider retailer range this version introduces, since a genuinely useful benefit provides little value if staff are not aware of what has actually changed since they last checked it.

Closing note

A simple, genuinely useful discount scheme is a small but real way Alderbridge supports staff day to day, and the wider range in this version exists to make that benefit even more useful.
